p: Alice Holt has been a working forest for an awfully long time. In Roman times, potters set up here, using the local clay and plentiful wood to fire their kilns, and their wares travelled across southern Britain. Centuries later, the forest's oaks were grown with the Royal Navy in mind, to build the wooden warships that once ruled the seas. It's a nice bit of history to share with kids as you walk among the trees.

Today the forest is home to Forest Research, the science arm that studies Britain's woodlands, so it's still very much a place where people work to understand trees. Thrill-seekers can try Go Ape's high-wire treetop course, booked separately, while cyclists will find a family-friendly route through the woods. The forest is also home to plenty of wildlife, from birds to butterflies in summer, with the quieter corners usually best for spotting them.

Allow at least two hours with little ones, half a day if you're doing the full marble run and a picnic. Bring a spare pair of socks for the kids if it has been raining, and a few coins or a card for parking.

There's lots nearby to round off the day. Frensham Common and its great ponds are a short drive away, with sandy shores and heathland walks. The Rural Life Living Museum at Tilford gives a hands-on peek at old country trades. And back in Farnham, the castle keep, the Georgian streets of Castle Street and some excellent independent cafés make a handsome end to your trip.
